# Model preset selection (model-profiles)

Use `list_node_model_presets` to check which presets are available with the installed backends and signed-in accounts.

| Family | Representative presets | Recommended uses |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Opus | `claude-opus` | Complex design, requirements, code review, decisions that need long context, and default Seo Soyoung and Seo Soyoung (PAS) sessions |
| Claude Sonnet | `claude-sonnet` | Quick research, card assignment decisions (`card-orchestrator`), and moderately difficult support tasks |
| Codex Sol | `codex-6.2-sol` | Backend and frontend implementation, tests, debugging, and refactoring |
| Codex Luna | `codex-6-luna` | Finding code quickly, simple fixes, and short one-off investigations |
| Gemini Carbon / Argon | `gemini-4-carbon`, `gemini-4-argon` | Reviewing many documents or screens at once, writing, and comparing alternatives from several perspectives |

## Choose a preset

1. Choose among presets marked `available: true` on the current node, with the backend installed and signed in.
2. If the user specifies a model or backend, use it.
3. Otherwise, consider higher-reasoning presets first for complex decisions and review. Start with lightweight presets for narrowly scoped research or support tasks.

catalog.ui_practice.body.title: CATALOG.md
catalog.ui_practice.body.content:
# Web and app UI guidelines (ui-practice)

Use these guidelines when building, changing, or reviewing a screen. Each shard covers recurring review findings and relevant public guidance from Vercel, WAI-ARIA APG, Apple HIG, Fluent 2, GOV.UK, NN/g, Refactoring UI, MDN, web.dev, Every Layout, and Radix.

## Order of precedence

1. Follow the project's canonical tokens, components and compositions registered in the review window, and shell block responsibilities. See the common rules in `ui-design.md` §1, §3, and §10 and the project's design guidelines.
2. Follow decisions recorded in this catalog when they differ from public guidance.
3. Use public guidance where the project and catalog are silent. Check whether project tokens meet the guidance before introducing any new CSS values.

Meet all eighteen requirements in `ui-design.md` §0 before starting. The shards apply those requirements to individual screens and controls.

## Choose the relevant shards

Read every shard that covers your changes. For a new screen, read shards 1–5 and any additional shards for the controls you use.

| Change | Shard |
|---|---|
| Layout, panes, width, responsiveness, spacing, alignment, radii, borders, and surfaces | layout-spacing |
| Text size and hierarchy, contrast, wrapping, truncation, numbers, copy length, and wording | text-copy |
| Scroll regions, scrollbars, overflow, sticky headers and footers, and long lists | scroll-overflow |
| Loading, empty states, errors, updates, flicker, layout shifts, and notification placement | states-feedback |
| Focus, keyboard, text selection, pointer and touch, IME input (such as Korean, Japanese, or Chinese), safe areas, and virtual keyboards | interaction-platform |
| Inputs, multiline fields, search, numbers and dates, selection, checkboxes, switches, segments, and sliders | controls-input |
| Buttons, icon buttons, toolbars, menus, context menus, dialogs, sheets, popovers, tooltips, tabs, and toasts | controls-action |
| List rows, tables, trees, card grids, drag and drop, images, media, and links | collections-media |

## Common UI mistakes

Check these ten issues before handing over a screen.

1. Side margins or gaps are too wide or too narrow (layout-spacing).
2. Surfaces with the same role use different materials, glass effects, or opacity (layout-spacing).
3. A local change redraws the whole screen and causes flicker (states-feedback).
4. Edits in another pane or newly sent messages take time to appear (states-feedback).
5. Text is too small (text-copy).
6. The screen has too much metadata or repeated copy (text-copy).
7. Different screens use different components for the same entity (collections-media, controls-action).
8. Gaps and padding vary between elements at the same level (layout-spacing).
9. Supporting text has the same weight as body text (text-copy).
10. A standalone action uses a text button where an icon button belongs (controls-action).

For mockups and published pages, use Awwwards and FWA award winners as the quality benchmark. Inspect screenshots and revise until they meet it.

## Source references

Square brackets cite these sources.

| Citation | Source |
|---|---|
| Vercel | https://vercel.com/design/guidelines , https://github.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines |
| APG pattern name | https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/ (dialog-modal, combobox, menu-button, tabs, slider, listbox, grid, treeview, toolbar, tooltip, switch, radio) |
| HIG page name | https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/ (layout, typography, buttons, text-fields, sheets, menus, toolbars, sliders, popovers, alerts, accessibility) |
| Fluent | https://fluent2.microsoft.design/components/web/react/core/ (field, dialog, menu, toolbar) |
| GOV.UK | https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/ (text-input, textarea, date-input, select, button, error-summary, pagination) |
| NN/g | https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ (form-design-placeholders, error-message-guidelines, skeleton-screens, infinite-scrolling-tips, indicators-validations-notifications) |
| RUI | Refactoring UI, https://medium.com/refactoring-ui/7-practical-tips-for-cheating-at-design-40c736799886 |
| MDN property name | https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/ (user-select, touch-action, overscroll-behavior, scrollbar-gutter, text-wrap, word-break, overflow-wrap, font-variant-numeric), KeyboardEvent.isComposing |
| web.dev | https://web.dev/articles/optimize-cls , https://web.dev/blog/viewport-units |
| EL | Every Layout, https://every-layout.dev/layouts/ (stack, sidebar, switcher) |
| Radix | https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/ (dialog, dropdown-menu, context-menu, popover, tooltip, slider, toast) |
| WCAG | https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/quickref/ |
| MWG guide ID | Chrome Modern Web Guidance, https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance . The guides use CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The MWG entries paraphrase that guidance. Use `retrieve` in the common `modern-web-guidance` skill to read the originals. |

Use the section number in references, following `ui-design §number` and `design-principles §number`. The review findings record recurring issues. The recommendations in each shard cover the principles behind those findings.

catalog.ui_practice.shard.layout_spacing.title: layout-spacing: layout, spacing, and surfaces
catalog.ui_practice.shard.layout_spacing.content:
# layout-spacing: layout, spacing, alignment, and surfaces

## Layout

Do
- Use flex, grid, and intrinsic layouts. Let the browser calculate sizes [Vercel "Let the browser size things"].
- Set sibling spacing on the parent with `gap` or Stack's `> * + * { margin-block-start }`. Nest a tighter Stack inside a looser one to distinguish spacing within groups from spacing between groups [EL stack].
- Use the Sidebar pattern for primary and secondary panes. Give the secondary pane a `flex-basis` and the primary pane a large `flex-grow` and a `min-inline-size`. Stack them when the primary pane would otherwise be too narrow [EL sidebar].
- Use the Switcher pattern to switch equal-weight panes from a row to a column together [EL switcher].
- Base the layout on the space the pane actually receives. A narrow panel still has narrow children in a wide viewport [EL sidebar].
- Let the main content (list, document, editor, or grid) fill extra space. Give one pane `flex: 1; min-height: 0` and keep toolbars, button rows, and section headers at their natural heights [Project guidelines].
- Keep features available in narrow windows. You can move secondary commands into a menu [HIG layout]. For a new desktop view, support narrow widths in the same PR or explain the limitation.
- Fill the available width. Center content with `max-width` inside a panel only where the design calls for it, such as to control line length in long prose [ui-design §5]. Lists, grids, and editors fill the width [Project guidelines].
- Reuse the existing screen frame for width, spacing, scrolling, and header and footer placement. Use the same markup and sizing contract for every route into the same screen [ui-design §6].
- Give symmetric panels the same resize behavior and minimum and maximum sizes [design-principles §9].
- Check wide, laptop, and phone widths. Use 50% browser zoom to simulate an extra-wide screen [Vercel "Responsive coverage"].
- Let users drag dividers between adjacent panes (folder, list, detail, and chat). Set a default width that keeps list text readable, with a generous resize range.
- Size panes and cards to their content. Give cards with similar amounts of content similar sizes.
- Keep the same structure and order on web and app. Adapt the input method to the platform [ui-design §6].
- If a mockup is approved, compare it side by side with an implementation screenshot and record missing elements and visual differences. Use real folders and names in mockups.

Avoid
- Fixed row or pane heights that clip enlarged text [HIG layout]. Shrinking spacing to hit a target height [ui-design §8].
- Layouts chosen solely by device name or portrait or landscape orientation [HIG layout].
- Screen-specific CSS that compensates for defects in shared components [ui-design §7].
- Giving a large share of the layout to a pane that is often empty [Project guidelines].
- Layouts that require horizontal scrolling (see scroll-overflow).
- Adding only whitespace on wide screens. Add panes or columns to maintain density.
- Wrapping several short values (node, agent, model) to two lines and loosening the layout.

Review findings
- Keep the same screen consistent on web and app.
- Use the full client area and keep the layout responsive.
- Give the left pane a readable default width and a draggable divider.
- Keep card and document lists from overlapping on the same screen.

## Spacing

Do
- Use spacing tokens. Use one value per level across the screen and increase it with the hierarchy. Spacing within a group < between groups < between regions [ui-design §4].
- Assign each space to one owner. The frame owns outer spacing and pane gaps, groups own internal gaps, and buttons own their size. Avoid stacking parent padding, child margin, and extra padding for the same space [ui-design §11].
- Use less space between a label and its input than between fields [EL stack].
- Keep outer left and right margins symmetric. Set horizontal and vertical spacing independently [ui-design §11].
- Separate surfaces with space, background color, or a subtle shadow first. Use borders as a last resort [RUI, ui-design §3].

Avoid
- Extra space at the bottom where the last child's margin adds to the container padding [EL stack].
- Cramping components by shrinking internal padding to hit a total height [ui-design §0 item 3].
- Different gaps at the same level, elements pressed against edges or neighbors, and elements that appear isolated.

Review findings
- Check for incorrect side margins and excessive gaps between elements.
- Keep size, spacing, and alignment consistent across screens of the same type.
- Check that uneven top and bottom spacing does not make a screen hard to read.

## Alignment

Do
- Align each element deliberately to a grid, baseline, edge, or optical center [Vercel "Deliberate alignment"].
- Use a single left starting edge and right ending edge per screen. Align the first header button, title, section headers, and card edges on the left. Check the right edge on elements with a visible end, such as boxes or rules [ui-design §5].
- Match the height and vertical center of elements in a row (chips and buttons, icons and text, badges and text) [ui-design §5]. If you change one element's sizing, list its siblings in the same row and container and check that they share the contract [ui-visual-integrity §3].
- Align top edges and first-line baselines across adjacent columns and cards.
- If measured alignment still looks wrong, adjust optically by about 1px [Vercel "Optical alignment"]. Match the weight of a thin stroke icon next to medium-weight text by adjusting stroke or size [Vercel "Balance contrast in lockups"].
- Use one alignment per group. Align digits in numeric table columns.
- Left-align chat, lists, and body text. Center only short single lines such as empty-state notices.
- In diagrams, align nodes and keep their spacing, arrow lengths and attachment points, and internal padding consistent. Keep labels clear of other elements.

Avoid
- Relying on DOM bounds alone. Line height, blank lines, or minimum heights can make bottom spacing look wrong even when padding matches [ui-design §11, ui-visual-integrity §2].
- Judging alignment from a crop of just the changed element. Capture the screen region it belongs to in one frame [ui-visual-integrity §1].

Review findings
- Left-align all chat messages, including previously centered ones.
- Line up the left edge of names precisely.
- Give chips and add buttons in the same row equal heights so their vertical centers align.
- Align connectors and arrow lengths, attachment points, and node spacing in diagrams.

## Corner radii, borders, and surfaces

Do
- Subtract the gap from the frame's radius to get the radius of a nested element. Keep the child radius at most the parent's. A radius at least half the element's height produces a pill shape [Vercel "Nested radii"].
- Use the same material for surfaces with the same role (sheets, panels, chat messages, and card frames) [ui-design §0 item 7].
- Cast shadows downward as if the light comes from above. Layer ambient and direct shadows. If you combine a border with a shadow, use a translucent border to keep the edge crisp [RUI, Vercel "Layered shadows", "Crisp borders"].
- On a tinted surface, use the same hue for borders, shadows, and secondary text [Vercel "Hue consistency", RUI].
- Give hover, pressed, and focused states more contrast than the resting state [Vercel "Interactions increase contrast"].
- Give lines and icons that identify controls and their states (input borders, checkmarks, and focus rings) contrast above 3:1 against adjacent colors. Apply this even to subtle glass borders when they are the sole clue to the control [WCAG 1.4.11, MWG color].
- Zoom in on glass effects at the corners of cards and large panels. Check for folded refraction or mismatched lens shapes.

Avoid
- Three or more nested borders, or a border between surfaces that are already distinct [ui-design §3, RUI].
- A fully opaque surface over a glass surface, or a text bubble so transparent that the background shows through [ui-design §0 item 7].
- Square selected chips inside pill-shaped frames or square item highlights that reach the edge of a rounded menu.
- A uniform halo produced by increasing only blur and spread [RUI].
- Using shadows, background images, or gradients alone for borders, dividers, or states. Forced colors removes these cues. Add a transparent `border` or `outline` [MWG color].
- Unexplained elements such as tiny corner squares, blurred text, glints, or dashed lines. Remove them or match the canonical design.
- Changing platform-native colors and standard shapes, such as iOS bubble and button colors.

Review findings
- Match materials such as Liquid Glass across screens.
- Avoid repeated frames and crowding screens with small elements and text.
- Keep refraction from folding at card corners.
- Remove unexplained squares from parent card corners.

catalog.ui_practice.shard.text_copy.content:
# text-copy: typography, wrapping, and UI copy

## Size and hierarchy

Do
- Choose sizes by role (page title, section header, card title, body, metadata, or badge). Match the token of neighboring elements with the same role [ui-design §2, §0 item 1].
- Use the body token for text users need to read, including button labels, inputs, checklist items, and descriptions. Reserve the metadata token for timestamps, counts, sources, and short tab labels. Use no smaller size [ui-design §2].
- Use weight and color as well as size to establish hierarchy. Use two weight ranges, 400–500 for body and 600–700 for emphasis, and 2–3 text colors [RUI]. Small bold text is common for section labels.
- Use secondary text tokens that exceed WCAG AA contrast against the background (4.5:1 for body text). Check screenshots in dark and light themes [WCAG].
- Let rows and panels grow when users enlarge text with browser zoom or Dynamic Type [HIG typography].
- Keep text at the same size for the same role across screens. Match the editor, chat text, and chat input sizes.
- Use smaller, quieter text for supplementary information such as tool calls, response time, and cost.
- Use one canonical font family, or the platform system font in apps. Use the same family for headings and body text. Set the page's `lang` and choose font fallbacks for the content language to avoid isolated glyphs in a different typeface.

Avoid
- Shrinking body text and button labels on new screens to metadata size [ui-design §0 item 1].
- Light or thinner weights for small UI text [HIG typography, RUI].
- Neutral gray text on a tinted background when the result looks muddy. Adjust lightness within the background's hue [RUI].
- Encoding state with color alone. Add text or a shape [Vercel "Redundant status cues"].
- Links that blend into a tinted background, such as blue links in a blue bubble.

Review findings
- Check that redesigning or merging screens does not make text too small to read.

## Wrapping, overflow, and numbers

Do
- For Korean and other CJK copy designed to keep words together, use `word-break: keep-all`. For English prose, use normal wrapping and enable `hyphens` where appropriate. Add `overflow-wrap: anywhere` for long unspaced URLs and identifiers [MDN word-break, overflow-wrap].
- Constrain variable-length titles, descriptions, chips, and names with single-line truncation (`text-overflow: ellipsis`) or a line limit (`line-clamp`). Set a maximum width for chips too [ui-design §5].
- Give flex children `min-width: 0` so they can shrink or truncate. Without it, one long word can push out the whole pane [Vercel].
- Use `text-wrap: balance` for short headings and `text-wrap: pretty` for prose to reduce single-word lines [MDN text-wrap].
- Use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for numeric columns meant for comparison and for changing values [MDN font-variant-numeric, Vercel].
- Keep numbers with their units and shortcut keys together (`10 MB`, `⌘ K`) [Vercel].
- Format dates, times, and numbers for the user's locale with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and `Intl.NumberFormat` [Vercel].
- Check the layout with very short, typical, and very long user text [Vercel "Resilient to user-generated content"].
- Limit line length for reading material such as card bodies, chat, and reports, even on wide screens.
- Reserve space for growing numbers such as card numbers and counts.

Avoid
- Text clipped at an edge without an ellipsis, or text overlapping other elements [ui-design §5].
- Using `word-break: break-all` as the default for body text. It breaks Korean and English in the middle of words [MDN word-break].
- Applying `white-space: nowrap` to long passages [MDN text-wrap].
- Setting a line limit taller than the container so the ellipsis falls on a hidden line. Match the container height to the line limit.
- Three periods (`...`) in place of the single ellipsis character `…` [Vercel].

Review findings
- Keep card lists narrow enough to read without scanning long rows.
- Check the layout with long question card descriptions.
- Check that long text wraps on mobile without overflowing.

## UI copy

Do
- Review every piece of visible text, including titles, descriptions, help, labels, buttons, empty states, errors, tooltips, and data-driven text. Ask whether users need it, whether it can be shorter, and whether it can be less prominent [ui-design §0 item 9].
- Remove generic labels such as "Section" and "List" when the layout already shows the structure.
- Start with short inline help. Use a tooltip as a last resort [Vercel "Inline help first"].
- Use verbs that describe what the button does, such as "Save", "Delete", or "Upload". Replace vague labels such as "Confirm" or "Continue" with the result [HIG alerts, Vercel, Project guidelines §2].
- Explain what went wrong and how to fix it in error messages [NN/g error-message-guidelines, Vercel].
- End menu items that open another window and in-progress messages with an ellipsis, such as "Rename…" and "Saving…" [Vercel].
- Use a single domain term for each concept. Keep implementation terms such as run out of the UI [Vercel "Keep nouns consistent"].
- Mark brand names, code, and identifiers with `translate="no"` to protect them from automatic translation [Vercel].
- Collapse supporting information, such as tool calls and cost, into chips that users can expand.
- Start reports and analysis pages with conclusions, charts, and figures. Put the methods and caveats in a collapsed section at the bottom. Include numbers in conclusions, charts, and tables (ui-design §0 item 10).
- Render Markdown and HTML with formatting intact inside chat messages and previews.
- Sanitize HTML from users, agents, and external sources, including HTML rendered from Markdown. Use `setHTML()` or DOMPurify in browsers that lack it. Keep unsanitized strings out of `innerHTML` and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` [MWG sanitize-untrusted-html].

Avoid
- Rows of summary tiles above the content that announce selections, counts, or section contents. Avoid rows of cards with oversized numbers and tiny labels immediately below a title [ui-design §0 item 10].
- Turning all available information into text or describing in prose what an image or layout already shows.
- Placeholder instructions that give no useful information, such as "Enter text here" [Project guidelines §3].
- Empty states and errors that repeat the same fact in several phrases [Project guidelines §5].
- Showing internal chat messages such as cache warmups, relays to other sessions, or start and end markers.
- Showing raw output such as JSON or event dumps. Format it for the chat view.
- Applying an imported title case rule to every English label. Follow the product's casing convention and use sentence case for English copy unless the product specifies otherwise.

Review findings
- Remove extra metadata from the screen.
- Avoid repeating facts such as the project name in the header and description.

catalog.ui_practice.shard.scroll_overflo.title: scroll-overflow: scrolling and long lists
catalog.ui_practice.shard.scroll_overflo.content:
# scroll-overflow: scrolling, overflow, and long lists

## Scroll regions

Do
- Use one scroll region per pane. Keep the title and toolbar above it and the action row and input below it. Scroll only the content between them [Project guidelines §1, §4].
- Let adjacent panes scroll independently. Make long explanations, lists, and descriptions scroll within their pane so users can reach the end.
- Keep navigation at the top of long pages with `position: sticky`.
- Open chats at the bottom, where the newest message is.
- If a newly opened item is offscreen, scroll only far enough to show it (`scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" })`). Leave the scroll position alone if the item is already visible.
- Clip scrollable content to the shape of a rounded frame.
- Use the project's scrollbar style, a thin overlay that appears when needed. Keep the full-page scrollbar available [ui-design §0 item 5].
- Fix overflow so only useful scrollbars appear. On macOS, set "Show scroll bars" to "Always" to see what Windows users see [Vercel "No excessive scrollbars"].
- If a scrollbar's appearance changes column widths, reserve space with `scrollbar-gutter: stable`. Overlay scrollbars take up no gutter [MDN scrollbar-gutter].
- If a thin overlay scrollbar makes the end hard to see, show an edge shadow or fade only while there is more to scroll in that direction. Remove it at the end [MWG scrollability-affordance-hints].
- Set `overscroll-behavior: contain` on scroll regions inside modals, sheets, and drawers so the background page stays still at the scroll boundary. Lock background scrolling separately [MDN overscroll-behavior, Vercel].
- To disable rubber-band scrolling only on desktop, set `overscroll-behavior: none` on `<html>` inside `@media (pointer: fine)` [Vercel].
- Preserve the user's scroll position after updates, sorting, and redraws. Restore the prior position on Back [Vercel "Scroll positions persist"].
- Use `scroll-margin-top` on anchor targets to keep sticky headers from hiding them [Vercel].
- Keep sticky headers and footers clear of focused elements [Vercel].

Avoid
- Exposing unstyled browser scrollbars [ui-design §0 item 5].
- Parent and child regions that both scroll in the same direction. Users cannot tell where the wheel will stop.
- Height limits that create nested scroll regions in reading material such as quotes and code. Leave these blocks expanded.
- Setting `overscroll-behavior: none` on every mobile page. It removes pull to refresh and swipe to go back [Vercel, MDN overscroll-behavior].
- Resetting scroll to the top or bottom in code and losing the user's place.

## Horizontal overflow

Do
- Fit lists, tabs, and cards in the visible width. Avoid wasting space on fixed side margins.
- Scroll wide tables horizontally within their own region. Keep the first column and header sticky.
- Keep a toolbar on one line and move excess commands into an overflow menu. If a single toolbar cannot fit at the minimum window width, split it into two [Fluent toolbar, Project guidelines §4].
- When a button row wraps, move whole groups to the next line [Project guidelines].

Avoid
- Tab rows or lists that rely on horizontal scrolling. Use horizontal scrolling only where explicitly approved.
- Hiding clipped content with `overflow-x: hidden` on a parent. Fix the cause, such as a missing `min-width: 0` or a fixed width [Vercel].

## Long lists

Do
- Default to infinite scrolling. Append the next page when users reach the end. Show a skeleton there while loading, a message and retry action on failure, and nothing at the end of the last page. Start from page one when the search query changes [Project guidelines §13].
- Public guidance also recommends pagination for finding and revisiting a known result, such as an item in search results or an audit log. In these screens, keep infinite scrolling and make the position recoverable. Put it in the URL and restore it when users return [NN/g infinite-scrolling-tips].
- Virtualize lists longer than 50 items (`virtua`, `content-visibility: auto`) [Vercel]. Preserve the scroll position and focus when virtualizing.
- In bottom-up lists such as chat, follow new messages only when users are already at the bottom. If they are reading earlier messages, preserve their place.

Avoid
- Building app-specific "Show more" buttons, page numbers, or "Showing M of N" lines. Avoid ending the list after the first few items with a count key or expression [Project guidelines §13].
- Redrawing the whole list while fetching the next page, causing flicker or jumping to the top (see states-feedback).

catalog.ui_practice.shard.states_feedbac.title: states-feedback: loading, errors, and updates
catalog.ui_practice.shard.states_feedbac.content:
# states-feedback: loading, empty states, errors, updates, and notifications

## Loading

Do
- On first entry, during screen or tab transitions, and while waiting for data, 3D content, or media, render the final layout first. Use the project's skeleton or progress indicator where the loaded content will appear [ui-design §0 item 13].
- Match skeleton layout and dimensions to the final content. Replace each skeleton in place without shifting anything [Vercel "Stable skeletons", NN/g skeleton-screens].
- To avoid flashing the loading indicator for fast responses, wait 150–300ms before showing it and leave it visible for at least 300–500ms once shown [Vercel].
- Keep the button label and width while loading. Add only the progress indicator [Vercel "Loading buttons"].
- Reserve space for images, embeds, and late-loading content with `width`, `height`, `aspect-ratio`, or a minimum height [web.dev optimize-cls].
- On failure, replace the loading indicator with an error in the same place [ui-design §0 item 13].
- Use background color and motion to distinguish running, preparing, and finished states without requiring users to read a label. Show a running child on its parent too.
- Show a thinking indicator in the chat bubble position while waiting for a response. Remove it when the response ends.

Avoid
- Showing only "Loading" outside the layout, such as in the top left, or leaving a blank screen [ui-design §0 item 13].
- Skeleton rows or images that differ in size from their final content and shift the screen when replaced [web.dev optimize-cls].
- Inserting content above what users are reading when loading finishes [web.dev optimize-cls].

Review findings
- Remove markers such as beginning and end from chat. Leave out elements that do not belong in a typical chat app.
- Keep the window width steady before and after loading.

## Empty states and errors

Do
- Design for empty, sparse, full, and error states. Keep the layout intact with empty strings or arrays [Vercel "All states designed"].
- State the current condition in one line (for example, "No new posts") and offer the next action. Center the message in its pane [Project guidelines §5].
- Put errors and sign-in prompts at the center of the pane that uses the affected source. Keep the rest of the screen available [Project guidelines §5].
- Say what is needed and how to fix the error. Preserve entered values so users can correct only the failed field. State server errors without blaming users [NN/g error-message-guidelines].
- Put form errors next to their fields and move focus to the first error on submit [Vercel, GOV.UK error-summary].
- Give every screen a next action or recovery path [Vercel "No dead ends"].
- If authentication expires, send users to sign-in instead of displaying fetch errors in every pane.
- Leave failed work in the list with a failed status and a message.

Avoid
- Blank areas that look broken and empty states that repeat the same fact [Project guidelines §5].
- Showing an error on an untouched field simply because it lost focus [NN/g error-message-guidelines].
- Putting a form error users must fix only in a toast that disappears after a few seconds [NN/g indicators-validations-notifications].
- Removing failed work from a list as though it succeeded.

Review findings
- Match post-action messages to what actually happened, such as the result of moving a card to a different status.

## Updates and flicker

Do
- Update every pane showing the same entity immediately, whether the change comes from another pane, a sent message, or an arriving result. Keep manual refresh out of the flow.
- Update only what changed. After a mutation, replace the relevant cached item optimistically with `setQueryData`. If invalidation is unavoidable, invalidate only that entity's key.
- Apply changes likely to succeed to the screen first, then reconcile with the server response. On failure, show an error and revert the change or offer undo [Vercel "Optimistic updates"].
- Preserve open dialogs, in-progress forms, and expanded panes while data updates in the background.
- Close dialogs explicitly when the action should dismiss them. Keep those that should stay open in place during updates. Check both success and failure.
- Give list items stable keys so the same DOM survives updates and preserves focus, scrolling, and expansion.
- Ask before leaving if there are unsaved changes (`beforeunload`, router guard) [Vercel].

Avoid
- Invalidating the whole list after a write, causing it to flicker twice a few seconds later.
- Showing a new item twice after an optimistic update and the server response.
- Closing and reopening an entire dialog for a single confirmation.
- Shifting layout and pane widths or rendering a blank screen between views when expanding, switching to edit mode, or changing screens or items.
- `transition: all`. List only properties you animate, such as `opacity` and `transform` [Vercel].

Review findings
- Keep the full list from redrawing repeatedly a few seconds after switching projects.
- When users save an edit in one pane, update other panes showing the same entity immediately.
- Keep chat and scene transitions free of blank frames and avoid layout changes where possible.

## Notifications and stacking order

Do
- Place notifications according to urgency and the action users need to take. Prefer inline status, use toasts for nonblocking notices, and reserve dialogs for required responses [NN/g indicators-validations-notifications, HIG alerts].
- Announce asynchronous results and validation with `aria-live="polite"` [Vercel, MDN aria-live].
- Use canonical layer tokens for toast > modal > overlay > panel. Check that a toast can appear above a modal.
- Confirm irreversible actions such as deletion or give users a safe window for undo. Skip confirmation for actions users can easily reverse [Vercel, HIG alerts].
- If the server disconnects, show one notice in its designated location.

Avoid
- Arbitrary `z-index` values.
- Modal alerts on app launch or for routine information [HIG alerts].
- Using a transient toast to ask a question that requires an answer [Radix toast].
- Sending notifications for actions users just took, such as completing a session awaiting review.

Review findings
- Keep error popups visible above large windows and panels.
- If the server disconnects, route users to the disconnection screen.
- Use a banner at the top or bottom of the screen when a banner is sufficient.

catalog.ui_practice.shard.interaction_pl.title: interaction-platform: input and accessibility
catalog.ui_practice.shard.interaction_pl.content:
# interaction-platform: focus, keyboard, text selection, pointer, touch, and mobile

## Focus and keyboard

Do
- Make every flow work from the keyboard. Follow APG focus and key behavior for composite controls [Vercel, APG].
- Use `:focus-visible` to show focus during keyboard navigation. Match the project's focus style, as used by the chat input. Use `:focus-within` for the outer border of a grouped input [MDN :focus-visible, ui-design §0 item 6].
- Give focus rings enough contrast on accent backgrounds. If you change the ring, check an accent button, link, toggle, and slider in the same view.
- Move focus inside a dialog, menu, or sheet when it opens. On close, return it to the trigger or a nearby element if the trigger is gone [APG dialog-modal, Project guidelines §12].
- On desktop, you can autofocus when the screen has one primary input [Vercel "Autofocus for speed"].
- If a search result or link opens an item on another screen, navigate to its position and show it selected.
- Keep editing active when users click a scrollbar or press Space. Move the cursor out of the field when editing ends.

Avoid
- The browser's default rectangular focus outline in a rounded design [ui-design §0 item 6].
- Removing focus with `outline: none` without a replacement [Vercel, MDN :focus-visible].
- Forcing focus order with a positive `tabindex` [APG dialog-modal].
- Autofocusing on entry on phones, which opens the keyboard and pushes the screen up [Vercel].
- Keyboard shortcuts designed only for QWERTY. Show the platform's shortcut symbols (⌘ or Ctrl) [Vercel].

## Text selection

Do
- In app screens, enable selection only for content. Use `user-select: none` for buttons, tabs, menus, chips, toggles, toolbars, control bars, canvas overlays, sortable table headers, selectable list-row labels, badges, field labels, and section labels [ui-design §0 item 11].
- Use `user-select: text` for readable or copyable content such as body text, code, errors, identifiers, and results. Use `user-select: all` for short values copied as a whole if appropriate [MDN user-select].
- On document pages, keep default selection and disable it only for interactive controls [ui-design §0 item 11].
- If a clickable row contains document text, allow selection by dragging. Clicking or double-clicking must leave text unselected, and ending a drag must leave the row action idle [ui-design §0 item 11].
- When dragging a slider, resizing, or dragging an item, disable selection in that region and set `inert` on the dragged element. Restore both when the drag ends [Vercel "Clean drag interactions"].
- Use the project's canonical selection policy when available (for example, `selection.css`).

Avoid
- Page-wide `user-select: none` that blocks copying [MDN user-select].
- Selection that starts in body text and highlights controls as the user drags across them.
- Text selection when users double-click or rapidly click controls [ui-design §0 item 11].

## Pointer and touch

Do
- Align the visible control and hit target. If the control is smaller than 24px, expand its target to at least 24px. Use at least 44px on phones [Vercel]. Apple recommends 44×44pt [HIG buttons].
- Give checkboxes and radio buttons one hit target spanning the label and control. Make every area that looks clickable respond [Vercel "No dead zones"].
- Use `touch-action: manipulation` on touch controls to prevent double-tap zoom. Choose `-webkit-tap-highlight-color` deliberately [Vercel, MDN touch-action].
- Give buttons and links visible hover and pressed states [Vercel, HIG buttons].
- Provide click and keyboard alternatives to drag, swipe, and pinch gestures [Vercel "Gestures have alternatives"].
- Use `touch-action` to set the browser-handled axis before a drag. Handle `pointercancel` in the same cleanup path [MDN touch-action].
- Use `<a href>` for navigation to support ⌘/Ctrl+click, middle-click, and opening in a new tab [Vercel "Links are links"].
- Let users drag or swipe horizontally through lanes. Snap to a pane boundary on release with `scroll-snap-type`.

Avoid
- Page-wide `touch-action: none` that disables zoom [MDN touch-action].
- Clickable `div` or `span` elements. Use `<button>` for actions [Vercel].
- Moving neighboring panes along with the item being dragged or swiped.
- Showing the browser's context menu (Back, Reload, Inspect) on app screens. Where there is no app menu, right-click should do nothing [Project guidelines §12].

Review findings
- Keep selection semantics consistent across ways of choosing the same item, such as selecting a photo in a list or tapping its map icon.

## IME input

Do
- Before handling Enter to send or select, check `event.isComposing` (or `keyCode === 229`) and skip the action during composition. Track composition with `compositionstart` and `compositionend`. This applies to input methods such as Korean, Japanese, and Chinese [MDN isComposing, compositionend].
- Leave arrow keys and Enter to the IME during composition, including in autocomplete and suggestions.
- Trim leading and trailing whitespace before saving. Avoid errors caused by spaces added by an input method [Vercel "Text replacements"].

Avoid
- Sending when Enter commits the last character or candidate. This can send twice or leave the final character behind [MDN isComposing].
- Blocking text entry in number fields. Accept input and explain validation errors afterward [Vercel "Don't block typing"].

## Mobile and native

Do
- In edge-to-edge layouts, pad controls with `env(safe-area-inset-*)`. Let backgrounds reach the edge while keeping titles, back and close controls, inputs, and save buttons and their hit targets outside system areas [MDN env, safe-area guidelines].
- Assign safe-area padding to the screen frame, navigator, or inner panel. Derive it from insets to avoid the status bar instead of using a fixed offset.
- Use `svh` for stable height or `dvh` for current height. With `100vh` alone, the browser bar can hide bottom buttons [web.dev viewport-units].
- Use at least 16px text for web inputs on phones to prevent iOS Safari from zooming on focus [Vercel].
- Match the keyboard layout with `inputmode` (numeric, decimal, email, tel, url, search) and the action key with `enterkeyhint` (search, send, next, done) [MDN inputmode, enterkeyhint].
- Keep the input and send button visible when the virtual keyboard opens. After opening a detail view from a list, press Back and check that you return to the same list. Close a modal and check that the original screen returns.
- Give swipe-to-dismiss screens a button with the same result [HIG accessibility]. Include a back button on child screens.
- Align back and action buttons in the app header with status bar icons.
- When the interface splits into two panes, as on an unfolded device, align buttons to their pane edges and use the available space.
- In dark themes, set `color-scheme: dark` on `<html>` and match `<meta name="theme-color">` to the background. Set the background and text colors for native `<select>` in Windows dark mode [Vercel, MDN color-scheme].
- If `prefers-reduced-motion` is set, reduce motion and convey the same information another way [MDN prefers-reduced-motion].

Avoid
- Disabling zoom with `user-scalable=no` or `maximum-scale=1` [Vercel].
- Assuming `100dvh` excludes the virtual keyboard [web.dev viewport-units].
- Passing a review based only on a default harness with zero safe-area insets. Check the real screen frame with nonzero top and bottom insets.

Review findings
- Keep the active line visible above the virtual keyboard when an input grows to several lines.
- Check that other elements do not obscure main content such as a map at mobile widths.

catalog.ui_practice.shard.controls_input.title: controls-input: input and selection controls
catalog.ui_practice.shard.controls_input.content:
# controls-input: input and selection controls

For all inputs, provide a visible `<label for>` that focuses the input on click. Connect help and errors with `aria-describedby`. Match the text token of nearby inputs with the same role (such as the chat input), use the project focus style, use at least 16px text on phones, and allow paste. Ignore Enter as an action key during IME composition, including Korean, Japanese, and Chinese input (see interaction-platform).

## Single-line input

Do
- Use a short noun for the visible label, such as "Title" or "English" [GOV.UK text-input, Project guidelines §3].
- Set the appropriate `type`, `name`, and `autocomplete` tokens for the field (name, email, current password, new password, or `one-time-code`) [MDN autocomplete, Vercel].
- For emails, codes, and usernames, set `spellcheck="false"` and disable automatic capitalization [Vercel].
- Match field width to the expected value length [HIG text-fields].
- Center the text vertically [ui-design §0 item 4].
- Use placeholders for an example value or format (`sk-0123…`) [Vercel].
- Make it clear how to apply a value. Provide a confirmation button or show that changes apply immediately.
- Let users click a title or description to edit it in place. Save on blur and revert on Escape. Keep the edit and save actions in the field.

Avoid
- Using placeholders as labels. They disappear on input and leave the field's purpose unclear [NN/g form-design-placeholders, Project guidelines §3]. Exceptions are toolbar search boxes and chat screens with one clearly identifiable writing field.
- Calling `preventDefault()` in `onPaste` [Vercel].
- Disabling autocomplete across all fields. Disable it only where password managers should stay out, such as search [MDN autocomplete, Vercel].

Also check
- Leave enough top padding inside the input to keep the text clear of the edge.
- If a value needs live updates, apply it immediately without a delay of seconds.

## Multiline input

Do
- Start the chat input at one line and grow it with the text. Scroll internally at its maximum height. Center text vertically in the empty state too [ui-design §0 item 4]. Start a primary field for long instructions, such as card assignment, at about three lines.
- Resize as the user types and respond to Send immediately. After sending, clear the field and reset its height.
- Keep Send in the same position as the field grows and after sending.
- Let the main editor fill the available height [Project guidelines §3]. Put comment or message inputs at the bottom of their pane.
- Soulstream uses Enter for a line break and Shift+Enter to send on web and app. Keep shortcuts consistent across the product. Also accept ⌘/Ctrl+Enter to send, as Vercel recommends for multiline fields.
- Keep selection chips and Send at their original size and position as the input grows [ui-design §8].
- Preserve drafts after errors and when users leave and return to the screen [GOV.UK textarea].
- Match standard editor behavior for cursor movement, multiline selection, cut and paste, and formatting shortcuts such as Ctrl+B.

Avoid
- The browser's default resize handle. Disable it with `resize: none` [ui-design §3].
- Text pushed into the upper left of an empty field [ui-design §0 item 4].
- Wide multiline fields for single-line responses such as a name or phone number [GOV.UK textarea].

Also check
- Grow fields such as notes with the text during editing.

## Search

Do
- Use `type="search"` or `inputmode="search"`, set `enterkeyhint="search"`, and put a named clear button at the end [MDN inputmode, HIG text-fields].
- If you show suggestions, use an editable combobox. Down Arrow enters the list, Enter selects, and Escape closes it. Keep focus in the field and reference the active option with `aria-activedescendant` [APG combobox].
- When no results match, state that in one line and suggest a different query or clearing filters [NN/g error-message-guidelines].
- Put the search field at the top. Keep its position and the result area's height stable as the result count changes [Project guidelines §1].
- Update results as users type. Run expensive full-text searches after a pause or on Enter.

Avoid
- Intercepting Left Arrow, Right Arrow, Home, End, and text input when suggestions are open [APG combobox].
- Giving the search field a password-like `name` that triggers password managers [Vercel].

## Numbers and dates

Do
- Use date and time controls for dates and times. Store ISO values and use null for an empty value [Project guidelines §3].
- Use a number field with stepper buttons for small integers [Project guidelines §3]. For decimals, use `inputmode="decimal"` [MDN inputmode].
- Use text for numeric identifiers such as postal codes and account numbers to keep leading zeroes [MDN inputmode].
- Use `Intl` to format values for the user's locale [Vercel].
- For new input types, test opening the picker with empty and invalid values. An empty date can blank the whole screen.

Avoid
- Advancing focus automatically when a field reaches its expected length [GOV.UK date-input].
- Blocking text input in numeric fields. Accept the input and show validation afterward [Vercel].

Also check
- Provide basic controls such as a date picker, time picker, and number stepper.

## Selection controls (select, combobox, dropdown)

Do
- Use a selection control when users must pick from a defined set. Use segments for 2–5 options, a dropdown for more, and autocomplete for more than a few dozen or when typing a name is faster [Project guidelines §3].
- Use a select or combobox for values and a menu for commands [Fluent menu].
- Support Up Arrow, Down Arrow, Home, End, and typeahead. Typeahead is especially helpful above seven options [APG listbox].
- Reposition the open list to avoid clipping at screen edges [Radix dropdown-menu `avoidCollisions`].
- Make the open list at least as wide as its trigger. Truncate long options with an ellipsis.
- Set background and text colors explicitly for native `<select>` in Windows dark mode [Vercel].
- Get defaults for creation dialogs and pickers from the current context, such as parent folder settings, favorites, or nearby dates.
- Keep options that are currently hard to use, such as a model at its limit, visible and selectable. Show the status beside the name.

Avoid
- Links, checkboxes, or buttons that can be operated independently inside an option [APG listbox].
- Repeating a long prefix on every option. Use a group label [APG listbox].
- Letting the page scroll behind an open picker and detach it from its trigger.

Also check
- Use the same default selection rule on web and app, such as the starred item.
- Keep unavailable options selectable and mark their names in red.
- Clear checkbox selections after a select-all bulk action.

## Checkboxes, radio buttons, switches, and segments

Do
- Allow one selection in a radio group. Tab enters on the selected option and arrow keys move between options [APG radio].
- Give switches `role="switch"` and `aria-checked`, and keep the same label in both states, such as "Receive notifications". Apply changes immediately without a separate Save button [APG switch, Project guidelines §1 Settings].
- Use radio semantics for segments that choose a value and tabs for segments that switch the panel below. Choose by behavior [APG radio, tabs].
- Give the label and control one hit target [Vercel].
- Use segments for filters on the same data, such as all, to do, and done [Project guidelines §6].

Avoid
- Adding a third state to a switch. Use the mixed state of a checkbox for partial selection [APG switch].
- Giving every radio button its own Tab stop [APG radio].

## Sliders

Do
- Give the thumb `role="slider"`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuenow`. Add `aria-valuetext` when units matter. Arrow keys move one step and Home and End move to the limits [APG slider].
- Separate preview while dragging from commit on release (Radix `onValueChange` and `onValueCommit`) [Radix slider].
- Add a numeric field when precision matters [HIG sliders].
- Set the drag axis with `touch-action`. Keep nearby text unselected during dragging [MDN touch-action, user-select].
- Use a thumb target larger than the visible thumb (at least 24px, or 44px on phones) [Vercel].

Avoid
- Moving the thumb without updating the value [APG slider].
- Giving both thumbs of a range slider the same name [Radix slider].
- Selecting text or scrolling the page while dragging.

Also check
- For marked sliders, verify that the thumb aligns with the tick marks.
- For time values, provide a slider and a precise input.

catalog.ui_practice.shard.controls_actio.title: controls-action: buttons, menus, and overlays
catalog.ui_practice.shard.controls_actio.content:
# controls-action: buttons, toolbars, menus, overlays, tabs, and toasts

## Buttons and icon buttons

Do
- Use `<button>` for actions and `<a href>` for navigation [Vercel, MDN button].
- Use the shared icon button for standalone actions such as Create, Expand, Edit, Star, and Settings (web v3 `DashboardIconCap`). Give it an `aria-label`, a tooltip, and `aria-pressed` if it toggles [Vercel].
- Use a text button with a verb for an action that finishes the screen's task, such as uploading, saving, or dismissing [Project guidelines §2].
- Keep buttons in a row the same size and shape. Group text buttons and icon buttons in separate rows [ui-design §3].
- Emphasize one primary action per screen, or at most two [HIG buttons, Project guidelines §2].
- Align the button row to the end and put the primary action last. Leave space between destructive and primary actions [Project guidelines §2].
- Disable unavailable actions and leave them visible so the row stays stable. Keep form submission enabled before the request and show missing fields on submit [Project guidelines §2, Vercel "Don't pre-disable submit", GOV.UK button].
- Disable the button when its request starts and show progress next to the existing label to prevent duplicate submissions [Vercel "Submission rule"].
- Follow direction conventions, such as a down arrow to expand and an up arrow to collapse. Match icons for the same action on the screen.
- Keep button labels unselectable during a drag or double-click [ui-design §0 item 11].
- Keep circular icon buttons the same width and height. Keep the row from flattening them into ovals.
- Choose icons from the canonical set of monochrome line icons and use theme colors.
- Put a copy icon button next to copyable values such as code blocks, quotes, identifiers, and dialogue on web and app.

Avoid
- A new text button when a shared icon button exists.
- Emoji or color images in place of icons.
- Buttons that fill a pane horizontally. Size them to their label.
- Chips or badges as large as buttons, or chips with inconsistent size and padding.
- Adding a border to only one button in a row, such as Delete.
- Duplicate entry points for the same action on one screen. Check for an existing action first.
- Button labels that leave the result unclear, such as "Confirm" or "Yes" [HIG alerts].
- A clickable `div` [Vercel].

Review findings
- If text buttons are crowding the interface, use round icon buttons for standalone actions such as Settings and the light/dark mode toggle at the top right.

## Toolbars

Do
- Keep the toolbar height constant across window sizes. Keep it on one line and move excess commands into a labeled overflow menu [Project guidelines §4, Fluent toolbar].
- Group related commands with spacing and separate destructive commands [Fluent toolbar].
- Give a toolbar with at least three controls `role="toolbar"` and a name. Enter it with one Tab stop and move within it with arrow keys [APG toolbar].
- Keep toolbars and action rows outside the scroll region [Project guidelines §0].

Avoid
- Wrapping a single toolbar to two lines. If it will not fit at the minimum window width, split it into two toolbars [Project guidelines].
- Several toolbar inputs that also need arrow keys for their own behavior [APG toolbar].

## Menus and context menus

Do
- For entities with state, such as cards and sessions, provide a menu or button path to every state reachable from the current one.
- Use the same menu items for an entity wherever it appears (session, work item, project, document, or row). If a new screen exposes an entity, fill in the entity-by-surface table and check for missing menus and create, edit, and delete paths.
- Collect actions already available in that context. Leave out actions the row already performs on click, such as opening or showing details [Project guidelines §12].
- Set `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded` on menu buttons. When Enter or Space opens the menu, focus the first item. Support typeahead [APG menu-button, Radix dropdown-menu].
- Align menus and popovers to the left edge of the trigger and size them to their content. Flip only to avoid clipping. If opened from the keyboard, place the menu below the row or above it if space is tight [Radix, Project guidelines §12].
- Close the menu on an outside click or Escape.
- Use one- or two-word verb phrases. End items that open another window with an ellipsis, as in "Rename…" [Fluent menu, Vercel].
- Mark destructive items and confirm the action with the target name visible. Place destructive items after other items [Project guidelines §12].
- Set the item radius to the menu radius minus its internal padding [Project guidelines §0].
- Open context menus by long press or keyboard as well (Shift+F10 or the Menu key) [Radix context-menu, Project guidelines §12].

Avoid
- Different menus for the same entity in different places.
- Several levels of nested submenus [Fluent menu].
- Closing a menu when the pointer moves slightly outside it.
- Menus in forms that collect values. Use selection controls [Fluent menu].
- Selecting the row as a side effect of right-clicking it [Project guidelines §12].

Review findings
- Add context menus wherever they are useful.
- Make create, edit, and delete available through the context menu in the project view on the left.

## Modal dialogs

Do
- Use a modal to confirm an action that's hard to undo, collect one short input, or make a selection. Use panes or tabs for extended editing and browsing [Project guidelines §7].
- Set `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, and `aria-labelledby` pointing to the title. On open, focus the first input or a safe action such as Cancel if there is no input. Keep Tab inside and return focus to the trigger on close [APG dialog-modal, Radix dialog, Project guidelines §7].
- Close on Escape. For a loss-confirmation alert, require a button to close [APG dialog-modal, Fluent dialog].
- Lock background scrolling and set `overscroll-behavior: contain` on the inner scroll region [Vercel, MDN overscroll-behavior].
- Size the dialog to its content. If it overflows, keep the header and buttons fixed and scroll the body [Fluent dialog, Project guidelines §7].
- Name the action or ask the question in the title. Use a verb on the confirmation button and always provide Cancel [Project guidelines §7, HIG alerts].
- Show errors and toasts triggered inside the dialog above it, using the canonical stacking order.

Avoid
- Giving initial focus to a destructive confirmation [Project guidelines §7].
- Setting `aria-modal` while leaving background clicks and keyboard interaction active [APG dialog-modal].
- Closing a dialog and discarding edits with one outside click.

Review findings
- Check that content-heavy dialogs such as Settings and questions do not overlap or collapse.
- Minimize a text editor on outside click so it stays open.
- Bring existing modals into line with these rules and avoid arbitrary mid-gray backgrounds.
- Provide confirmation and cancellation where appropriate in agent, node, and model pickers.

## Sheets and drawers

Do
- Use Done to save, Cancel to close without saving, and Back to go to the previous step [HIG sheets].
- For modal sheets, use the same focus management and background lock as dialogs. Set `overscroll-behavior: contain` [shadcn sheet, MDN overscroll-behavior].
- Provide a close button even if the sheet supports swipe to dismiss [HIG accessibility].
- Keep buttons above safe areas and the virtual keyboard in mobile bottom sheets (see interaction-platform).

Avoid
- Stacking sheets. Use a full screen or separate window for long, complex tasks [HIG sheets].
- Share sheets or bottom sheets that always cover the screen. Size them to their content and buttons.

## Popovers and tooltips

Do
- Open tooltips on hover and keyboard focus and close them on Escape. Delay the first in a group and show subsequent nearby tooltips immediately [APG tooltip, Vercel "Tooltip timing", Radix tooltip].
- Use popovers for supporting surfaces with inputs or buttons [APG tooltip, Radix popover].
- Preserve work if an outside click closes a popover. Discard only on explicit cancellation [HIG popovers].
- Match the size and radius of existing popovers with the same role.

Avoid
- Focusable links or inputs inside a tooltip [APG tooltip].
- Putting essential help only in a tooltip. Provide short inline help [Vercel "Inline help first"].

## Tabs

Do
- Use tabs for 2–7 peer views. Name each with a short noun that describes its panel [Project guidelines §6].
- Connect `tablist`, `tab`, and `tabpanel`. Move with arrow keys. For panels that take time to display, activate with Enter or Space [APG tabs].
- Store the selected tab in the URL so it survives refresh, sharing, and Back [Vercel "URL as state"].

Avoid
- Using tabs for ordered steps [Project guidelines §6].
- A count summary below the tabs or title [Project guidelines §6, ui-design §0 item 10].
- A tab row that requires horizontal scrolling.

## Toasts and notifications

Do
- Use toasts for nonblocking notices. Pause auto-dismiss on hover, focus, or when the window loses focus [Radix toast].
- If a toast offers Undo, provide another way to undo the action [Radix toast].
- Put toasts at the top of the stacking order so they remain visible above modals.

Avoid
- Using only a toast for a required answer or a form error users must fix [Radix toast, NN/g indicators-validations-notifications].

Review findings
- Keep the filter bar from taking up too much space.

catalog.html_design_preset.body.title: CATALOG.md
catalog.html_design_preset.body.content:
# Design presets for standalone HTML pages (html-design-preset)

Choose one of three presets: `index`, `apple`, or `astryx` for a standalone HTML report, dashboard, or introduction page. Keep colors, materials, corners, shadows, and component styles within that preset. Use `compile_subtree` to read only the selected preset's shard at its `node_id`.

## Choose a preset

1. If the user names Index, Apple, or Astryx, use that preset.
2. For a new document without a specified preset, use `index`.
3. If you are editing or expanding a document and the user hasn't requested a redesign, keep the preset in the root's `data-design` attribute.
4. If the user requests multiple presets or the choice is ambiguous, ask which single preset to use.

## Preset characteristics

| Preset | Root attribute | Suitable documents |
|---|---|---|
| `index` | `data-design="index"` | Ledger-style status reports, check results, assessment summaries, and decision rationale. Put conclusions first and let readers expand supporting evidence as needed. Use a white background, rules, and spacing, with square corners and no shadows. |
| `apple` | `data-design="apple"` | Product introductions, showcases, image-led presentations, and long explanations read from start to finish. Use scale and spacing for hierarchy, and reserve translucent materials for floating controls. |
| `astryx` | `data-design="astryx"` | Dense, scannable tools such as operations consoles, monitoring dashboards, and metrics views. Use semantic tokens and restrained surfaces. |

## Shared requirements

- Support light and dark themes and respect `prefers-color-scheme`. Adapt the same hierarchy to dark mode without inverting the colors.
- Use text of at least 13px. For Korean and other CJK text that should keep words together, use `word-break: keep-all; overflow-wrap: break-word`. For English prose, use normal wrapping and enable `hyphens` where appropriate.
- Make the document open as a single file without external CDNs or images. Fall back to a system font stack.
- Define raw colors, sizes, radii, and spacing only in the root token block. Use `var()` in rules.
- Draw structures and flows in SVG or HTML and CSS. Replace ASCII diagrams and raw Mermaid source.
- Prefer tables, diagrams, and visual hierarchy to prose descriptions.
